files_reviewed: grep of every src/app/api route.ts for requireAuth
note: Next.js plus Prisma plus OpenAI helpdesk. The model call runs on the server, so no ai_browser_call. Middleware only checks that the owly-token cookie has three dot-separated parts and does not verify the signature. Routes that skip requireAuth are therefore reachable with a forged cookie such as a.b.c. Twilio SMS and phone routes do check signatures.

labels.what: blockedTopics (legal, medical, investment advice, price commitments, competitor comparisons) is defined with checkBlockedTopics, but engine.ts never imports or calls it, and enforceResponseLength (line 66) is also unused. The rule is not enforced anywhere
Prompt says never make up information not in the knowledge base. Nothing in the tools or reply path checks answers against it

requiresHumanApproval flags refund, cancellation, discount, compensation and legal messages but only writes metadata to the conversation. The model still answers and can still call tools. No approval step exists
send_internal_email sends real SMTP mail from model-chosen to, subject and body with no approval step
trigger_webhook posts a model-built payload to a configured external URL with no approval
send_internal_email accepts any recipient address. No allowlist of team addresses, no rate limit, so a customer can steer it into mailing outside addresses
assign_to_person updates any ticketId the model passes, with no check that the ticket belongs to this conversation
create_ticket writes title, description and priority with no length cap, enum check in code, or per-conversation limit
get_customer_history reads any customerId or contact the model passes. A customer can ask for another person's history. No check against the current conversation owner
schedule_followup stores nothing and sends nothing. It returns success and a scheduled time while a code comment says a queue would be used. The model tells the customer a follow-up is booked
schedule_followup returns scheduled success with no job record, so the customer message never goes out

The page and API gate only checks that a cookie exists and has three dot parts, or that any x-api-key header is present. The JWT signature is never verified here, so a forged cookie passes for any route that does not call requireAuth

WhatsApp connect and disconnect have no requireAuth, only the weak middleware check. Anyone with a forged cookie can connect or disconnect the business WhatsApp session (also channels/email/route.ts lines 8-30)
The webhook test route has no requireAuth and fetches a stored webhook URL with the stored headers
The realtime stream has no requireAuth and lets the caller pick any channel name from a query param, so a forged cookie can listen to message events

POST /api/chat has no requireAuth and no per-IP chat limit beyond the general API limit. It takes any conversationId from the body, so a caller can read or write another customer's conversation. Each call is a paid model run. The widget (public/widget/owly-chat.js line 111) calls it from the browser, but middleware blocks it without a cookie
Telegram webhook runs the model on any posted update with no secret-token check (SMS and phone routes validate Twilio signatures, Telegram does not)
/api/channels/phone, /sms and /telegram skip auth and the general rate limit entirely
Every API key gets admin role, with no scope. Keys are looked up in plain text by the key column
In-memory rate limit keyed on the x-forwarded-for header, which a client can set (getClientIp lines 53-59)
Knowledge base text and customer name are put into the system prompt with no separation or escaping
aiApiKey, twilioToken, smtpPass and telegramBotToken stored in plain text columns in Settings (API responses are masked by maskSettingsSecrets)
Seed script creates default admin and sample departments, team members and knowledge entries (not fully read)
Default admin user with password admin123 hardcoded and printed at line 162
maxResponseLength 2000, confidenceThreshold 0.6 and the keyword lists are constants in code, not settings
Database URL falls back to postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/owly
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL set to http://localhost:3000 (also helm/owly/values.yaml line 104)
Tool-call depth limit of 5 and message history of 50 (line 116) hardcoded
